hero.headline: FBI stops attack plot targeting White House UFC event
hero.body:
Federal authorities disrupted an alleged terrorist plot targeting a UFC event at the White House, the Justice Department announced. Five men were arrested across multiple states in connection with the conspiracy to attack the "Freedom 250" event.

The arrests took place over the weekend in Ohio, Missouri, Nebraska, and California. According to charges filed by the Department of Justice, the five men allegedly planned a coordinated assault involving both aerial and ground-based weapons.

The suspects reportedly intended to deploy drones armed with explosives around the UFC event to force an evacuation. Following the evacuation, they allegedly planned to position snipers to fire upon "high value targets" within the fleeing crowd.

Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche emphasized the swift response by law enforcement. "The FBI, our law enforcement partners and our U.S. Attorneys did what they do every day to make America safe through quick response and vigilance in investigating, disrupting, and dismantling this alleged plan before it could be carried out," Blanche said. He added that the administration would "take immediate and aggressive action to identify and prosecute those who incite and plan acts of violence."

Court filings unsealed by the government reveal that the group expressed grievances about various issues, including corruption, the Epstein files, and data centers. These motivations were cited in the charges against the men.

The investigation identified the conspiracy before the event took place, allowing authorities to prevent the planned operation. The UFC Freedom 250 event proceeded as scheduled after the threat was neutralized.

Security experts have pointed to this incident as evidence of evolving terrorist tactics. The use of drones equipped with explosives represents a method that law enforcement agencies increasingly monitor as a security concern.

The FBI led the investigation that uncovered the plot, working alongside other law enforcement partners and U.S. Attorneys' offices to build their case. The multi-state nature of the operation required coordination between federal agencies across different jurisdictions.

The incident highlights the security challenges posed by large-scale public events held at sensitive government locations. The White House decision to host the UFC event meant implementing enhanced security measures to protect attendees and government officials present.

The investigation remains active as officials work to determine whether additional individuals were involved in planning or supporting the alleged attack. Authorities continue to gather evidence and interview witnesses to establish the full scope of the conspiracy.

The successful disruption of the plot underscores the ongoing work of federal law enforcement to identify and prevent violent attacks before they occur. The charges represent the government's commitment to prosecuting those involved in planning violence against public events and officials.

cards.headline: US and Iran to Begin Nuclear Talks Friday Following Initial Agreement
cards.teaser: The United States and Iran will begin new negotiations on nuclear arms and sanctions relief on Friday, Iran's foreign minister announced Tuesday.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran will begin negotiations on nuclear arms and sanctions relief on Friday, following the signing of an initial agreement. President Trump stated he hopes to move past the conflict, while Iran's foreign minister confirmed the talks would proceed.

The deal includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz waterway, a key shipping route. Oil prices have fallen and stock markets have risen following the announcement. Iran has stated that any comprehensive agreement requires Israeli forces to withdraw from Lebanon as part of broader regional security discussions.

cards.headline: Trump announces permanent toll-free access to Strait of Hormuz under Iran deal
cards.teaser: President Trump declared the Strait of Hormuz will remain permanently toll-free under a new agreement with Iran, though most ships continue to avoid the waterway.
cards.body:
President Trump announced an agreement with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz with toll-free passage. According to Trump, the deal has been signed and full access is expected soon.

However, ships remain hesitant to transit the waterway. Security concerns, mines, and toll risks continue to pose obstacles to resuming traffic levels from before the conflict. The disruption has also affected fuel costs globally, with prices spiking when the conflict began in late February.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak Could Become Worst on Record, Africa CDC Warns
cards.teaser: Health officials say the outbreak could take a year to contain if infection rates continue at current levels.
cards.body:
The head of the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention warned that the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could become the worst on record if containment efforts fail to slow transmission rates.

About a month after the latest outbreak was identified, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, confirmed cases had reached 676 with 136 deaths, mostly concentrated in the DRC's Ituri province. According to the World Health Organization, the number of victims is roughly doubling every week.

The outbreak has created heartbreaking situations on the ground. When an orphanage in Bunia took in a newborn baby after his mother died from Ebola, staff members hoped to save his life. The infant survived only two weeks. Four nuns who cared for him subsequently fell ill with the virus. All children and staff at the orphanage are now being monitored for symptoms.

Health workers battling the outbreak face significant obstacles. Frontline responders report shortages of personal protective equipment and vehicles needed to transport bodies. While testing has improved, workers say it still needs to happen faster and closer to patients. In neighboring Uganda, which has reported 19 cases and two deaths, intensive contact tracing has kept the outbreak under control, according to health officials.

Community resistance poses another major challenge. Misinformation is spreading, with some people denying the virus exists or blaming aid organizations for spreading it. People are reluctant to allow sick relatives to receive care in healthcare isolation units, partly due to concerns about funeral rites. According to one study after the 2016 outbreak, unsafe funeral practices for Ebola victims created an average of 2.58 secondary cases per exposure to body fluids.

Dr. Jean Kaseya, director general of Africa CDC, highlighted a critical gap in contact tracing. With about 600 confirmed cases in one area, experts would expect to monitor roughly 24,000 contacts. However, only 4,955 contacts had been listed, with just 57 percent being monitored. Kaseya warned this represents a substantial risk for continued community transmission, noting that some confirmed cases remain outside hospitals.

Conflict in the worst-affected regions and attacks on aid workers and treatment centers are also slowing response efforts. A local MP for Bunia noted on social media that international funding pledges have not been sufficiently visible on the ground in Ituri.

A joint response plan by Africa CDC and the WHO estimates that 518 million dollars will be needed over six months to bring the outbreak under control. Kaseya said some early financial pledges were not fulfilled, but approximately 212 million dollars in funding and support in kind has been committed.

Scientists are developing vaccines against Bundibugyo, and existing antivirals show promise for treating the virus.

cards.headline: Trump Signals Return of Sanctions on Russian Oil at G7
cards.teaser: The president indicated sanctions would be reimposed as G7 leaders refocus attention on Ukraine.
cards.body:
President Trump indicated at the Group of Seven summit that oil sanctions on Russia would be reinstated as G7 leaders work to refocus attention on Ukraine's ongoing conflict. The move reflects a shift in U.S. policy toward Russian energy exports and represents a return to economic pressure measures used earlier in the war.

The announcement came as America's allies sought to prioritize Ukraine on Trump's agenda at the summit, following a period when other international crises had drawn attention away from the conflict.

cards.headline: Japan Raises Interest Rates to Highest Level in Three Decades
cards.body:
The Bank of Japan has raised its key interest rate to 1 percent, marking the highest level in 31 years as policymakers attempt to control inflation pressures linked to the Iran war. The central bank increased its short-term policy rate by a quarter percentage point from 0.75 percent, signaling a significant shift in Japan's monetary approach.

The decision reflects growing concerns about price pressures spreading through the economy. Bank of Japan officials warned that companies are passing on rising oil costs to each other at a relatively fast pace. Despite recent declines in oil prices following a U.S.-Iran peace agreement framework, the central bank proceeded with the rate increase, indicating confidence that inflationary risks warrant action even as immediate oil price pressures ease.

Central bank governor Shinichi Uchida acknowledged at a press conference that the signing of a U.S.-Iran memorandum was "a welcome move" while noting uncertainty about how quickly oil supplies would recover. He emphasized that while the risk of sharp economic deterioration from the Middle East conflict has diminished, underlying inflation concerns persist. With core inflation approaching the central bank's 2 percent target, officials said it was important to ensure that inflation stabilizes at desired levels.

The rate increase lifts Japan's borrowing costs to levels not seen since 1995, when the central bank was reducing rates following the collapse of asset prices in the late 1980s. This represents a dramatic turnaround from 2016, when Japan implemented negative interest rates in an effort to stimulate the economy and combat decades of deflation.

The move comes as major central banks respond to inflationary pressures. The European Central Bank recently raised its main interest rates, while the U.S. Federal Reserve and Bank of England are expected to hold borrowing costs steady at upcoming meetings. Japan's approach remains gradual compared to more aggressive tightening seen elsewhere.

The government has introduced a relief package to help households facing elevated fuel costs, which likely contributed to the central bank's confidence in proceeding with the rate increase. Higher borrowing costs will affect businesses and consumers across Japan, potentially moderating economic activity while helping to stabilize prices.

Markets reacted positively to the decision, with some investors viewing it as measured rather than hawkish. The Nikkei share index reached 70,000 points for the first time during Tuesday's session, closing at a new record high. The index has gained approximately one-third of its value so far this year.

The rate increase marks a watershed moment for an economy that spent much of the past three decades struggling with deflation and stagnation. Economists will monitor how Japanese businesses and households respond to higher borrowing costs and whether additional rate increases follow.

cards.headline: Kevin Warsh Leads First Federal Reserve Meeting as New Chairman
cards.teaser: The new Federal Reserve chairman faces decisions on interest rates and inflation as policymakers gather for their first meeting under his leadership.
cards.body:
Kevin Warsh is presiding over his first Federal Reserve meeting as chairman. The gathering addresses key issues including interest rate decisions, inflation management, and the Fed's institutional independence.

Warsh plans to break with tradition by withholding his own interest rate projection from the Fed's outlook, signaling caution about the economic trajectory. Most Fed officials are unlikely to forecast rate increases, though some may hint at the possibility of future hikes as policymakers assess monetary policy direction.

cards.headline: Group Planned Attack on White House UFC Event, FBI Says
cards.teaser: Federal authorities say suspects plotted to use snipers and drones in an attack on the event.
cards.body:
Federal authorities disrupted a planned attack on a UFC event at the White House, according to newly unsealed court filings. The alleged plot involved using guns and drones to target the cage fighting event held on Sunday.

Five people were arrested in a multi-state operation involving Ohio, Missouri, and California. Court documents reveal the group expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centers. Law enforcement intervened before the attack could be carried out.

cards.headline: Russian Warship Fires Warning Shots Near British Yacht in English Channel
cards.teaser: The UK Defense Ministry is investigating the incident involving a Russian frigate and a UK-registered yacht.
cards.body:
Britain's Defense Ministry is investigating reports that a Russian frigate fired warning shots near a UK-registered yacht in the English Channel. The Admiral Grigorovich, a Russian naval vessel operating in the Channel, discharged the shots after the yacht drifted toward it. Russia confirmed that its frigate fired the warning shots.

The incident marks a rare occurrence of Russian naval operations in waters so close to British territory, raising tensions in the busy waterway between Britain and France.

cards.headline: European Leaders Soften Tone Toward Trump at G7 Summit
cards.teaser: A peace framework with Iran and hope for Ukraine cooperation shifted the atmosphere in France.
cards.body:
European leaders took a more cooperative approach with President Trump at the Group of 7 summit in France on Tuesday. French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Trump on signing a new Iran agreement, reflecting improved diplomatic relations after previous tensions between the US and its European allies.

The warmer tone was supported by substantive discussions on global security. Trump met with G7 leaders alongside Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and representatives from Qatar and UAE during the summit's first full day. The meetings addressed Ukraine cooperation and Russian oil sanctions, signaling renewed collaboration on key international challenges.

cards.headline: German Broadcaster Removes TV Intro After Musk Legal Action
cards.teaser: ZDF responded to a cease and desist letter after Elon Musk condemned what he called outrageous lies.
cards.body:
German public broadcaster ZDF removed a television program introduction following a cease and desist letter from Elon Musk. The tech entrepreneur objected to what he characterized as "outrageous lies" in the broadcaster's content.

ZDF complied with the legal demand and pulled the introduction. The dispute reflects broader tensions between Musk and European media organizations over their coverage and statements.

cards.headline: Tropical Storm Arthur expected to form in Gulf of Mexico
cards.teaser: A tropical system in the western Gulf could develop into Tropical Storm Arthur by Wednesday morning as Texas prepares for the season's first named storm.
cards.body:
The National Weather Service issued a Tropical Storm Watch for parts of the Texas Gulf coast as forecasters track Potential Tropical Cyclone 1. The system could strengthen into Tropical Storm Arthur by Wednesday morning, threatening millions of residents along the coast.

Texas authorities are preparing for the arrival of the first named storm of the hurricane season. The developing weather system in the western Gulf has prompted warnings for coastal communities to monitor conditions closely and prepare for potential impacts from wind and rain.

cards.headline: Education Department shifts special education and civil rights oversight to other agencies
cards.teaser: The Trump administration moved oversight of special education to Health and Human Services and civil rights enforcement to the Justice Department as part of ongoing efforts to dismantle the Education Department.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump ordered the transfer of special education oversight from the Education Department to the Department of Health and Human Services, while shifting civil rights enforcement to the Department of Justice. These moves align with Trump's stated goal to close the Education Department entirely.

The restructuring significantly reduces the agency's scope and responsibilities, stripping it of two major operational areas. The transfers represent the latest step in the administration's effort to dismantle the department.

cards.headline: Twelve killed in Missouri skydiving plane crash
cards.teaser: A plane carrying skydivers crashed in Butler, Missouri, killing all twelve people on board, including a teacher, a cancer survivor, and a new father.
cards.body:
The victims of a fatal plane crash at a skydiving facility in Butler, Missouri have been identified. The aircraft, a Pacific Aerospace P750XL, was carrying nine experienced skydivers, two tandem jumpers and a pilot when it went down at Skydive KC over the weekend. Among those killed were a high school music teacher, a cancer survivor, and a new father with two young children.

Dr. Jen Sharp, a recognized leader in women's skydiving, was also among the 12 people who died in the crash. Family members have shared details about the victims, including one father expressing confusion about what caused the accident that claimed his son's life.

cards.headline: Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool turns green after blue paint treatment
cards.teaser: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool has turned green from algae growth despite a $14.2 million project to paint it American flag blue.
cards.body:
President Trump authorized a $14.2 million renovation project for the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, aiming to transform it into what he called a "beautiful" monument from its previous "filthy" and "dirty" state. The plan included painting the water American flag blue.

However, the project has faced an unexpected setback. Green algae have proliferated in the pool following the renovation, particularly amid warm weather conditions. The algae growth has turned the water green instead of the intended bright blue color.

cards.headline: Appeals court blocks release of Catholic sex abuse investigation report
cards.teaser: A New Jersey appeals court ruled that Seton Hall University does not have to disclose the full contents of an investigation into sex abuse allegations involving former Cardinal Theodore McCarrick.
cards.body:
Judges blocked the release of most of Seton Hall University's report examining allegations against former Cardinal Theodore McCarrick. The appellate court determined that privilege shields some investigative documents related to sex abuse litigation facing the Archdiocese of Newark.

The investigation was conducted by law firm Latham & Watkins into the Catholic Church abuse allegations. The court ruling means Seton Hall does not have to disclose the entirety of the probe's findings, protecting certain materials from public release despite ongoing litigation.

cards.headline: SpaceX to Acquire AI Company Cursor for $60 Billion
cards.teaser: SpaceX exercised its option to buy the artificial intelligence startup in an all-stock transaction following its recent public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX will acquire AI startup Cursor for $60 billion in an all-stock deal, exercising a purchase option it held on the company. The acquisition comes shortly after SpaceX's initial public offering and aims to strengthen the company's AI division.

The deal reflects SpaceX's focus on artificial intelligence, with the company telling IPO investors it sees a $26 trillion addressable market in AI. The $60 billion valuation represents one of the largest AI acquisitions in the technology sector.

cards.headline: European Union Approves Trade Agreement With United States
cards.teaser: After nearly a year of negotiations, EU lawmakers have given final approval to a trade deal struck with President Trump.
cards.body:
The European Parliament has approved a tariff agreement with the United States that was negotiated with President Trump last July. The approval came nearly a year after the deal was initially proposed, and just days before a July 4 deadline when the U.S. threatened to impose increased tariffs.

The parliament's approval came with two main conditions attached to the agreement. This final legislative step removes a major obstacle to implementing the trade deal between the EU and the United States.

cards.headline: Pizza Hut Sold to Two Companies for $2.7 Billion
cards.teaser: Yum China will acquire locations in mainland China while private equity firm LongRange Capital buys US and international restaurants.
cards.body:
Yum! Brands is dividing Pizza Hut between two buyers in a $2.7 billion deal. Yum China will take over Pizza Hut locations in mainland China, while private equity firm LongRange Capital will acquire restaurants in the United States and other markets.

The sale marks the end of Yum! Brands' ownership of the struggling chain, which has contended with outdated stores and intense competition. The company had considered selling Pizza Hut since February and planned to close 250 U.S. locations.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Warns AI Company Anthropic About Model Restrictions
cards.teaser: Commerce Secretary Lutnick sent a letter to Anthropic warning of potential curbs on top AI models as officials seek an agreement.
cards.body:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick sent a letter to Anthropic warning of potential restrictions on its powerful models as the Trump administration and the AI company negotiate over operating terms for advanced systems.

The conflict centers on Anthropic's Claude Fable 5, which the US government classified as a dangerous munition and restricted from access by foreign nationals. Unable to distinguish between American and foreign users, Anthropic suspended access to the model for everyone. Security experts warn that restricting individual models won't address the broader challenge posed by rapidly advancing AI capabilities.

cards.headline: Dow Jones Reaches Record High as Oil Prices Fall
cards.teaser: The Dow climbed 350 points to a new record as declining oil prices fueled optimism about economic conditions.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average hit a record high, climbing 350 points as oil prices declined following a U.S.-Iran deal announcement. President Trump stated that the agreement includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway, which prompted crude oil markets to respond with lower prices. The oil decline boosted investor confidence about economic conditions ahead.

The Nasdaq and S&P 500 experienced declines as technology and chip stocks faced pressure. SpaceX contributed to positive market momentum with news of an acquisition deal, providing some counterbalance to the technology sector's pullback.

hero.headline: Google releases Android 17 with new multitasking features and Wear OS 7 for smartwatches
hero.body:
Google has released Android 17 and Wear OS 7, introducing a range of productivity and AI-focused upgrades across its Pixel device lineup. The operating system updates are rolling out through over-the-air updates to Pixel phones and watches, with broader availability expanding in the coming weeks.

Android 17 brings several new multitasking capabilities designed to improve user productivity. The update includes floating "Bubble" app windows that make it easier to manage multiple applications simultaneously. A new Screen Reaction recording mode allows users to capture video of themselves and their screen at the same time, enabling them to create reaction videos popular on social media. The phone app has also been expanded with new functionality. Additionally, Android 17 introduces a 50/50 split gaming mode designed specifically for foldable phones.

The update incorporates enhanced parental controls and security tools to help families manage device usage more effectively. Google has indicated that major AI features will arrive later this summer through the accompanying Pixel Drop update, which brings the company's latest AI models to its devices.

Wear OS 7 targets smartwatch users with performance improvements and new capabilities. The update introduces Live Updates, a feature that tracks live events on Wear OS devices. This means users can monitor ongoing information like sports scores or meal delivery status directly on their smartwatches. The smartwatch operating system also delivers improved battery life, helping devices keep up with user activity throughout the day.

Wear OS 7 incorporates Gemini AI integration, extending Google's artificial intelligence capabilities to wearable devices. The update is rolling out to Pixel Watch 2, 3, and 4 models.

The releases continue Google's annual update cycle for its mobile and wearable platforms. Pixel devices receive the updates first, with other manufacturers expected to release Android 17 for their devices in the following months after completing customization and testing processes.

Google has not provided specific details about which individual Pixel models will receive the updates or confirmed exact timelines for global availability. The company noted that users should expect the over-the-air updates to arrive gradually as the rollout expands beyond initial Pixel device availability.

These updates represent Google's broader push to integrate artificial intelligence across its hardware ecosystem. The company is positioning the Android 17 and Wear OS 7 releases as improving both productivity and device longevity, emphasizing how new features can help users work more efficiently while maintaining the long-term health and performance of their devices.

cards.headline: Qualcomm developing chips for AI wearables including jewelry and camera-equipped earbuds
cards.teaser: The chipmaker is working on over 40 different AI wearable devices as it positions for a future computing platform beyond smartphones.
cards.body:
Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon announced Tuesday that the company is developing chips for over 40 AI wearable devices, including jewelry, camera-equipped earbuds, pins, and watches. The move demonstrates Qualcomm's strategy to position itself as a leading processor provider for the next generation of computing devices.

The initiative reflects an industry shift away from smartphone-centric interfaces toward distributed wearable technology. By establishing chip supply relationships across diverse wearable categories, Qualcomm aims to secure a dominant role in whatever computing platforms emerge to complement or replace smartphones in consumers' daily lives.

cards.headline: Security flaw in FIFA World Cup system could have allowed control of match broadcast streams
cards.teaser: A researcher discovered a vulnerability in FIFA's online platforms that provided access to internal systems including broadcast controls.
cards.body:
A security researcher discovered a flaw in FIFA's online platforms that granted access to internal systems controlling the television broadcast of World Cup matches. The vulnerability could have allowed unauthorized users to modify live streams viewed by millions of viewers worldwide.

The researcher reported the security issue after identifying the extent of access the bug provided to FIFA's broadcast infrastructure. The discovery underscores significant security vulnerabilities in the systems used to manage and deliver major sporting events to global audiences.

cards.headline: Pentagon reports using AI to generate congressional reports
cards.teaser: The Department of Defense says 1.5 million personnel are using generative AI tools, including for writing mandated reports.
cards.body:
The Pentagon disclosed it is using artificial intelligence to write reports required by Congress, while claiming that 1.5 million personnel across the department are now using generative AI tools. The announcement marks one of the first official confirmations of AI use for formal government reporting.

The disclosure raises questions about the role of automated systems in producing official government documents submitted to lawmakers. The Pentagon did not specify which reports involved AI generation or what level of human review the AI-produced content receives before submission to Congress.

cards.headline: NASA telescopes reveal formation history of ancient star cluster Terzan 5
cards.teaser: The Webb and Hubble space telescopes captured new observations of a relic from the Milky Way's early formation.
cards.body:
NASA released images and data from the Webb and Hubble space telescopes showing Terzan 5, a stellar structure considered a fossil fragment from the Milky Way galaxy's formation. The European Space Agency also published images of the bulge fossil fragment.

Terzan 5 sits near the Milky Way's central bulge and contains stars from multiple generations, making it valuable for understanding how the galaxy formed billions of years ago. The combined observations from both telescopes provide insights into the cluster's composition and history that single-telescope studies could not achieve.

cards.headline: Mobileye to launch US robotaxi service while supplying competitors
cards.teaser: The self-driving technology company will operate its own autonomous taxi service while continuing to sell systems to other robotaxi providers.
cards.body:
Mobileye plans to launch its own robotaxi service in the United States, putting the company in direct competition with some of its existing customers. The move reflects the company's ambition to capture a share of the robotaxi market itself.

This strategy creates an interesting dynamic in the autonomous vehicle industry, where Mobileye will simultaneously operate as both a technology supplier to other companies developing robotaxi services and as a competitor offering its own fleet-based service.

cards.headline: Rivian cuts hundreds of jobs after beginning R2 deliveries
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker reduced its workforce as part of restructuring meant to reach profitability.
cards.body:
Rivian has cut hundreds of jobs as part of a restructuring effort aimed at scaling toward profitability. The company made the decision following the start of R2 deliveries.

The automaker recently delayed its profitability timeline to increase investment in autonomous driving technology, adding pressure to balance growth initiatives with financial sustainability in a competitive industry.

hero.headline: Tottenham agree £52 million deal with Brighton for defender Jan Paul van Hecke
hero.body:
Tottenham Hotspur has reached an agreement with Brighton to sign Netherlands defender Jan Paul van Hecke for £52 million. The 26-year-old center back, who represented the Netherlands at the recent World Cup, is set to complete his move to the north London club.

Van Hecke has been a key figure in Brighton's defense and his performances at the World Cup drew attention from several top clubs. The Dutch international joined Brighton in 2020 and has made over 150 appearances for the Seagulls across all competitions. His consistency and aerial ability have made him one of the Premier League's most reliable defenders.

The transfer fee represents a significant investment by Tottenham as they look to strengthen their defensive options. The £52 million deal would make van Hecke one of the most expensive defenders in Spurs' history. Brighton has developed a reputation for developing talent and selling players for substantial profits, having previously sold defenders to top clubs.

Tottenham manager has prioritized defensive reinforcements after his team conceded goals during the previous campaign. Van Hecke's ability to play out from the back fits the style of play Spurs have employed. The defender is expected to undergo a medical examination in the coming days before finalizing personal terms.

The deal is subject to van Hecke agreeing personal terms and passing a medical. Brighton will now turn their attention to finding a replacement for the departing defender. Tottenham supporters will hope the Dutch international can help shore up a defense that has been inconsistent in recent seasons.

cards.headline: John Tortorella will not return as Vegas Golden Knights coach
cards.teaser: The Vegas Golden Knights announced that John Tortorella will not return as head coach following the team's loss in the Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights have ended their relationship with head coach John Tortorella. The decision comes after the team's run to the 2026 Stanley Cup Final, where they fell short of winning the championship.

Tortorella, who won a Stanley Cup with Tampa Bay in 2004, joined the Golden Knights before the 2025-26 season. The franchise is now searching for a new head coach.

cards.headline: Cameron Norrie loses on return from injury at Queen's tournament
cards.teaser: Britain's Cameron Norrie was defeated by Alejandro Davidovich Fokina at Queen's in his first singles match since suffering a rib injury in May.
cards.body:
Cameron Norrie's comeback from injury ended in disappointment at Queen's Club Championships, where he lost to Spain's Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the Round of 32. It was the British player's first singles match since sustaining a rib injury in May.

The defeat marks a difficult return to competitive tennis for the British number one as he prepares for Wimbledon later in the month.

cards.headline: Sri Lanka upset New Zealand at Women's T20 World Cup
cards.teaser: Sri Lanka delivered a shock five-wicket victory over defending champions New Zealand in the Women's T20 World Cup at Southampton.
cards.body:
Sri Lanka secured a historic victory over defending champions New Zealand in their Women's T20 World Cup match at Southampton, chasing down 153 runs with two balls remaining. The result marks the first time Sri Lanka has beaten New Zealand at a Women's World Cup.

Nilakshi de Silva delivered a commanding unbeaten 54 to lead Sri Lanka's successful chase. Kaushani Nuthyangana sealed the victory with a four, dealing a significant blow to New Zealand's title defense and opening up the tournament.

cards.headline: Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby sets Pro Day for July 10
cards.teaser: Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby has tentatively scheduled his Pro Day for July 10 as he prepares to enter the NFL supplemental draft.
cards.body:
Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby has scheduled his Pro Day for July 10 as he prepares to enter the NFL supplemental draft. The event will allow NFL scouts to evaluate his performance and abilities.

Sorsby's decision to pursue the supplemental draft pathway comes as he navigates an ongoing NCAA legal matter related to gambling allegations affecting college football.

cards.headline: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha gains 8 million followers after World Cup performance against Spain
cards.teaser: Cape Verde's 40-year-old goalkeeper Vozinha gained 8 million social media followers after his heroic performance helped hold Spain scoreless.
cards.body:
Vozinha, the 40-year-old Cape Verde goalkeeper, has seen his social media following surge by 8 million after his outstanding performance against Spain at the World Cup. The veteran keeper made a series of crucial saves to help his team earn a draw against one of the tournament favorites.

The result spoiled a $1 million bet and represented one of the biggest upsets of the tournament's group stage. Spain had been expected to easily defeat Cape Verde but were frustrated by Vozinha's heroics. Mikel Merino said Spain were mourning after the disappointing draw that cost them valuable points in their quest to top the group.

cards.headline: MLB players face backlash over Pride Night protest
cards.teaser: San Francisco Giants players are receiving criticism from multiple sides following their protest during Pride Night festivities.
cards.body:
Several San Francisco Giants players wrote Bible verses on their caps during the team's Pride Night event, sparking controversy. Major League Baseball issued a statement criticizing the players, noting that writing on caps violates league rules. The players have denied that their decision stems from a place of hate.

The incident occurred during a Giants home game as part of MLB's Pride Month celebrations in June. San Francisco, home to a large LGBTQ population, typically makes a significant effort to acknowledge the community during these events. The backlash over the protest has drawn attention from multiple perspectives across the political spectrum.

hero.headline: More Than 16,000 Sign Petition Urging Congress to Pass Anti-Deepfake Legislation
hero.body:
More than 16,000 people have signed an open letter from SAG-AFTRA calling on Congress to pass the NO FAKES Act, a revived bill that would ban unauthorized artificial intelligence-generated images and videos. The legislation would give individuals legal control over how their name and likeness are used in AI-generated content.

The petition comes as deepfakes have become increasingly common with the rise of large language models and generative AI tools. These technologies have made it easier to create realistic but fake depictions of actors, singers, and other public figures without their consent. The entertainment industry has raised concerns about the potential for unauthorized use of performer likenesses in everything from fake celebrity endorsements to synthetic performances.

The NO FAKES Act represents a legislative response to growing anxiety about AI's impact on personal identity rights. If passed, the law would establish federal protections for individuals whose images or voices are replicated by artificial intelligence without permission. The bill had been introduced previously but has been revived amid mounting pressure from the entertainment industry and advocacy groups.

SAG-AFTRA has made AI protections a central focus of its advocacy work, particularly following contract negotiations that addressed the use of AI in film and television production. The union has pushed for clear guardrails around the use of digital replicas and synthetic performances, arguing that performers should maintain control over their own images and voices throughout their careers and beyond.

The petition drive reflects broader concerns about the intersection of technology and personal rights in the digital age. As AI tools become more sophisticated and accessible, questions about consent, compensation, and control over digital likenesses have moved from theoretical concerns to immediate policy debates. The entertainment industry, with its concentration of recognizable faces and voices, has emerged as a focal point for these discussions about how to regulate AI-generated content while balancing innovation and individual rights.

The debate over AI-generated content highlights a larger pattern emerging across sectors as technology advances faster than legislation. Similar concerns about technology outpacing regulatory frameworks are appearing in other areas, from education to social media. As stakeholders across industries push for protective measures, policymakers face the challenge of creating rules that safeguard individuals while allowing technological progress to continue. The NO FAKES Act and similar legislative efforts aim to address this balance by establishing clear boundaries around the use of personal identity in AI applications, particularly in cases where individuals have not provided their consent.

cards.headline: UK Bans Social Media Use for Children Under 16
cards.teaser: The United Kingdom announced it will prohibit children under 16 from using apps including TikTok, Snapchat, and YouTube.
cards.body:
The UK government announced a ban on social media use for children under 16, with Prime Minister Keir Starmer saying the measure aims to give children their childhood back. The policy responds to growing concerns about social media's effects on young users.

The scope of the ban remains to be clarified, with questions about how it will apply to platforms like YouTube, Roblox, and WhatsApp. Actor Jeremy Allen White supported the move, stating the media industry needs a correction in how it addresses youth access to digital platforms.

cards.headline: Chris Brown Dog-Mauling Trial Delayed After Mistrial Declared
cards.teaser: A Los Angeles judge excused jurors and ordered a new trial to begin later this week.
cards.body:
A Los Angeles judge declared a mistrial in Chris Brown's dog-mauling case, citing misconduct by a panel member. The judge excused the jury and ordered Brown to return for the start of testimony in a new trial.

The new trial is scheduled to begin on Thursday. The case involves allegations related to an incident involving Brown's dog. The judge's decision to declare a mistrial means the proceedings will restart with a new jury panel.

cards.headline: Portland Restaurants and Bar Take Three James Beard Awards
cards.teaser: Three Portland establishments won honors at the 2026 James Beard Awards ceremony.
cards.body:
Portland's culinary scene earned recognition at the 2026 James Beard Awards ceremony, with local restaurants and a bar among the winners. The James Beard Awards rank among the most prestigious honors in the American restaurant industry.

Winners from Portland described the recognition as career highlights. The awards celebrated excellence across the city's dining and bar establishments.

cards.headline: Hugh Jackman to Star as Robin Hood in Michael Sarnoski Film
cards.teaser: The director of The Death of Robin Hood discusses casting Jackman and adapting Death Stranding for A24.
cards.body:
Director Michael Sarnoski has cast Hugh Jackman in The Death of Robin Hood, a darker reimagining of the legendary outlaw. Rather than a heroic figure who steals from the rich to help the poor, Sarnoski's version portrays Robin Hood as a selfish criminal who keeps stolen goods for himself. Jackman plays a dour version of the character, troubled by the romanticized tales told about him.

The film explores the gap between legend and reality, contrasting the fireside stories that herald Robin Hood with the truth known only to those whose lives he's actually touched. Sarnoski's revisionist approach offers a grittier take on the folk hero, departing significantly from previous portrayals by actors like Errol Flynn, Kevin Costner, and Sean Connery.

cards.headline: LaKeith Stanfield and Greg Kinnear Join Cast of Netflix Monsanto Legal Drama
cards.teaser: The actors join Jonathan Bailey and Laura Dern in John Lee Hancock's courtroom film about litigation against the chemical company.
cards.body:
LaKeith Stanfield, Greg Kinnear, Julia McDermott, David Duchovny, Melonie Diaz, and Bilal Hasna have joined the cast of John Lee Hancock's Netflix legal drama. The film stars Jonathan Bailey and Laura Dern in a story about the landmark trial against Monsanto.

The untitled film follows the true story of legal action against the U.S. chemical company. Hancock is directing the courtroom drama, which focuses on litigation that became a significant legal precedent. The cast additions bring additional star power to the project.

cards.headline: MrBeast Coin Flip Changed Outcome of Survivor Season 50
cards.teaser: The show's team discusses a moment created by YouTuber Jimmy Donaldson that altered the season's ending.
cards.body:
A coin flip created by YouTuber MrBeast, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson, changed the ending of the 50th season of CBS's Survivor. The show's host and contestants discussed the moment that altered the game's outcome.

The team behind Survivor explained how the coin flip mechanism worked and its impact on the competition. After 50 seasons, introducing elements that fundamentally change gameplay represents a significant shift for the long-running reality competition series.

hero.headline: Trump administration transfers special education and civil rights enforcement from Education Department
hero.body:
The Trump administration announced Tuesday that it is shifting special education programs and civil rights enforcement out of the Department of Education. The Department of Justice will take over civil rights enforcement and student privacy protection, while the Department of Health and Human Services will assume responsibility for special education initiatives for students with disabilities.

This reorganization represents a significant change in federal oversight of student protections. Civil rights enforcement has historically been handled by the Education Department, covering discrimination complaints related to race, sex, disability, and other protected categories in schools and universities. Student privacy protections under federal law, including regulations governing educational records, will now move to the Justice Department.

The decision affects millions of students with disabilities served under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, which guarantees eligible children access to free and appropriate public education. Moving these programs to Health and Human Services places them within an agency focused on health and welfare services rather than educational policy. This shift will impact oversight of funding, compliance monitoring, and technical assistance that schools receive for special education services.

The announcement aligns with the Trump administration's broader effort to restructure the Education Department, which the president has promised to close. The transfer of these core functions raises questions about how enforcement priorities and program administration may change under new agency arrangements.

The source material indicates that the administration has already begun shifting its approach to civil rights enforcement. The Education Department announced it had terminated agreements that previous administrations reached with five school districts and a college aimed at upholding rights and protections for transgender students. The affected districts include Cape Henlopen in Delaware, Fife in Washington, Delaware Valley in Pennsylvania, and La Mesa-Spring Valley, Sacramento City Unified, and Taft College in California. Under the Biden and Obama administrations, the department interpreted Title IX to include protections for transgender and gay students.

Kimberly Richey, assistant secretary for civil rights at the education department, said the action reflected the administration's view that prior administrations had imposed "unnecessary and unlawful burdens" on schools. She characterized the previous approach as a "relentless pursuit of a radical transgender agenda."

Al Goldberg, a Sacramento City Unified spokesperson, said it remains unclear what effects Monday's decision would have on the district's policies or funding, though the district stated it remains committed to supporting LGBTQ+ students and staff.

The administration did not provide a detailed timeline for completing the transfers or specify how staff and budgets would be reallocated. Schools, parents, and advocacy organizations will need to adjust to new points of contact and potentially different procedures as the reorganization takes effect.

cards.headline: Federal prosecutors charge 15 in Minnesota immigration enforcement obstruction case
cards.teaser: The Justice Department charged 15 people accused of impeding federal officers during immigration operations in Minnesota.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice charged 15 people Tuesday with conspiracy to impede or injure federal officers following their actions during an immigration enforcement operation in Minnesota earlier this year. US Attorney Daniel Rosen and Michael McCarthy, special agent in charge of Homeland Security Investigations for Minnesota, announced the charges at a Minneapolis press conference.

Prosecutors allege the defendants interfered with federal immigration enforcement agents carrying out their duties. According to the DOJ, the individuals are members or associates of Direct Action Minnesota and other groups that prosecutors say actively oppose law enforcement operations.

cards.headline: Justice Department adds charges against suspect in National Guard shooting
cards.teaser: An Afghan national faces eight additional federal charges in the November shooting of two National Guard members in Washington.
cards.body:
The Justice Department unsealed a superseding indictment Tuesday adding eight new charges against Rahmanullah Lakanwal in connection with the November shooting of two National Guard members patrolling in Washington. The new charges include murder of a person assisting a federal officer. Lakanwal pleaded not guilty to the additional counts.

The National Guard members were on patrol in the nation's capital when the shooting occurred in November. The superseding indictment expands the scope of federal charges against Lakanwal, who now faces multiple counts related to the attack on the service members.

cards.headline: FBI director says bureau stopped planned attack on White House UFC event
cards.teaser: The FBI thwarted an attack targeting a UFC event at the White House that President Trump attended, with suspects in custody.
cards.body:
FBI Director Kash Patel said Tuesday that the bureau disrupted a planned attack on the UFC event held at the White House on Sunday, which President Trump attended. Five people were arrested across multiple states, including Ohio, Missouri, and California.

According to unsealed court filings, the group allegedly planned to use snipers and explosive-laden drones to attack the event. The suspects expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centers.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats release drug pricing proposals ahead of midterm elections
cards.teaser: Senate Democrats unveiled a series of proposals to lower prescription drug costs as part of their midterm campaign strategy.
cards.body:
Senate Democrats released a blueprint of proposals Tuesday aimed at lowering prescription drug costs, positioning healthcare affordability as a central campaign message as they seek to retake control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections. High prescription drug prices remain a major concern for voters across party lines.

The Democratic proposals offer a counterpoint to President Trump's approach of voluntary pricing deals with pharmaceutical companies. Democrats are framing the contrast as part of their effort to distinguish their policy agenda from the White House on an issue that resonates with voters.

cards.headline: Senator Cornyn withholds support for Todd Blanche as attorney general nominee
cards.teaser: Senator John Cornyn declined to commit to supporting Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche's confirmation after meeting with him.
cards.body:
Senator John Cornyn of Texas met with Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche on Tuesday but stopped short of endorsing his nomination to permanently lead the Department of Justice. Cornyn described the meeting as a positive interview but said he would not make a confirmation decision until after a briefing and completion of Blanche's hearing before the Senate Judiciary Committee.

Cornyn's position indicates that Blanche may face questions during the confirmation process. As a senior Republican senator, Cornyn's support would be valuable for the nomination, making his wait-and-see approach noteworthy for the administration.

cards.headline: Macron and Zelensky caught on microphone discussing Trump at G7 summit
cards.teaser: French President Emmanuel Macron and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky were overheard on a live microphone talking about President Trump.
cards.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky were inadvertently picked up by a live microphone Tuesday while discussing President Trump at the G7 Leaders summit in Evian-les-Bains. The exchange came as the two leaders addressed tensions that had emerged during earlier talks with Trump over Ukraine policy.

The hot-mic moment highlighted ongoing efforts by G7 allies to keep Ukraine central to Trump's agenda. Recently, discussions about Iran have competed for attention with the ongoing war in Ukraine as world leaders gather to address global priorities.
